A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be [[Definition:Square Matrix|square matrices]] of [[Definition:Order of Square Matrix|order]] $n$ over $\R$.
Then:
:$\map \det {\mathbf A \mathbf B} = \map \det {\mathbf A} \map \det {\mathbf B}$

B_source.statement:
Let $S, T: \R^n \to \R^n$ be [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear transformations]].
Then the signed volume-scaling factor of $S \circ T$ is the product of those of $S$ and $T$.

validity_conditions: The determinant equals the signed factor by which a linear map scales volume (n-dimensional oriented measure).
Applying two maps in succession multiplies their scaling factors, and composition corresponds to matrix product.
So the multiplicativity of volume scaling transports directly to determinants.
proof_plan: From [[Area Scaling by Determinant]], $\map \det {\mathbf M}$ is the signed volume-scaling factor of the linear transformation $x \mapsto \mathbf M x$.
Composing linear transformations multiplies their scaling factors, since $S \circ T$ first scales by that of $T$, then by that of $S$.
By [[Matrix Product as Composition of Linear Transformations]], $\mathbf A \mathbf B$ represents the composition of the transformations represented by $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
